summary: The paper introduces CODEC, which applies sparse-autoencoder decomposition to hidden-neuron *contributions* (Integrated-Gradients-style attributions to scalar output targets) rather than activations, and validates the resulting modes causally via targeted ablation/preservation experiments on ResNet-50, with extensions to ViT-B and CNN models of retinal ganglion cells. The core idea — that contribution space is sparser, higher-dimensional, and progressively sign-decorrelated across depth, and that modes in this space identify necessary/sufficient channels better than activation modes — is genuinely interesting and supported by a reasonable causal perturbation analysis. However, the manuscript is weakened by sloppy writing (run-ons, typos, garbled math, an internal inconsistency of 200 vs 300 training epochs), an almost complete absence of error bars, seeds, or significance testing on the headline comparisons, and thin engagement with the modern SAE/mechanistic-interpretability literature. This is a sound, useful, borderline-accept submission whose deficiencies are fixable without new core experiments.
strengths: Novel and well-motivated framing: decomposing causal contributions (receptive x projective field composition) rather than activations addresses a real gap, and the completeness property of Integrated Gradients gives the per-channel scalarization a principled footing.

Causal validation rather than purely correlational claims: the ablation/preservation experiments (Fig. 6) directly test whether contribution modes identify necessary and sufficient channels, with target vs off-target accuracy curves and an area-based performance score across blocks.

Interesting, non-obvious empirical findings: contributions are sparser and higher-dimensional than activations, and positive/negative contributions progressively decorrelate with depth — a phenomenon with a plausible (and appropriately hedged) mechanistic interpretation.

Cross-domain generality demonstrated at least qualitatively: CNN image classifiers, ViT-B (with honest reporting of weaker results), and retinal CNN models where modes yield testable neuroscience hypotheses about dynamic receptive fields.
Reasonable robustness analysis of the SAE stage (threshold, dictionary size, L1, seed, non-negativity constraints) and a stated limitations section.

key_concerns.issue: No statistical treatment of the main results: sparsity/dimensionality/decorrelation trends (Fig. 3), class-correlation comparisons (Fig. 5), and perturbation efficacy (Fig. 6D-E) are reported without error bars, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the 'black widow' example is a single showcased class, and it is unclear whether the contribution-vs-activation gap is significant across all 1000 classes.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report means +/- std over SAE seeds and bootstrapped image subsets for Figs. 3, 5, 6; show the full distribution of the performance score across all classes (not one exemplar), with a paired test against activation-mode and random-channel baselines.

key_concerns.issue: Limited baseline coverage: the only comparison is contribution-modes vs activation-modes vs random channels. There is no comparison to other channel/neuron-selection or concept-attribution methods (e.g., TCAV-style concept vectors, Grad-CAM-guided channel selection, network-dissection-style rankings) for the ablation/preservation task, so the claim that CODEC is *better* at identifying causal channels rests on one baseline family.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add at least one or two established channel-ranking baselines (e.g., activation-magnitude ranking, Grad-CAM/IG channel importance, TCAV sensitivity) to the Fig. 6D-E perturbation curves.

key_concerns.issue: Writing quality is below ICLR standard: pervasive run-on sentences, typos ('selecte', 'retinl', 'non-labled', 'forinterpreting'), garbled math layout in the contribution-mapping section, and an internal inconsistency (training stated as both ~200 and 300 epochs in the same paragraph).
key_concerns.suggested_fix: A careful full editing pass; fix the epoch inconsistency and re-typeset the Jacobian/contribution-map equations.

key_concerns.issue: Thin positioning against the modern sparse-autoencoder interpretability literature: the prose cites Fel et al. (2023) but does not delineate CODEC from the large body of dictionary-learning/SAE work on transformer and vision activations, nor from feature-circuit analyses, which are the closest methodological relatives.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Add a related-work paragraph explicitly contrasting contribution-space decomposition with activation-space SAEs and circuit analyses, clarifying what is gained beyond applying SAEs to activations with post-hoc causal probes.

key_concerns.issue: Some methodological choices are underjustified: 10 IG integration steps is coarse, the top-logit scalar target is justified only by the vague phrase 'sufficient for an accurate reconstruction', the class-correlation threshold of 0.2 is arbitrary, and reconstruction R^2 ~0.85 leaves 15% of contribution variance unexplained with no analysis of whether the missing variance matters for downstream conclusions.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Justify or sweep integration steps; report sensitivity of Fig. 5 to the correlation threshold; analyze whether perturbation results hold when restricting to the reconstructed (mode-explained) component of contributions.

key_concerns.issue: The dangling claim 'we have at this point only analyzed scaling with LLMs (see supplemental material)' is unsupported by anything described in the main text and reads as an overreach toward generality.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either describe the LLM analysis concretely (even briefly) or remove the claim.

questions_for_authors: Across all 1000 ImageNet classes, what is the distribution (with variance over seeds/images) of the Fig. 6E performance score for contribution modes vs activation modes, and is the difference statistically significant?

How sensitive are the Fig. 3 sparsity/decorrelation trends and Fig. 5 class-correlation results to the number of IG integration steps and to the choice of scalar target (top logit vs top-k sum vs entropy)?
The SAE is trained with 200 epochs in one sentence and 300 in the next — which is correct, and do the reported trends depend on this?
Why is a correlation threshold of 0.2 used in Fig. 5C, and how do the counts change under reasonable alternatives?
For the retina analysis, the CNN has only 8 channels per layer — how many modes k were used, and is an overcomplete decomposition meaningful or even identifiable at this scale?
Does the 15% unexplained reconstruction variance correlate systematically with particular classes or channels, and could it bias the perturbation results?
calibration_check: Claims are mostly well scoped — the ViT weakness and block-limited analyses are openly acknowledged and the decorrelation explanation is hedged — but the abstract's generality framing and the unsupported LLM-scaling aside slightly outrun the evidence.

significance.justification: Contribution-space decomposition with causal validation is a useful tool that interpretability and neuroscience-of-ANN researchers would plausibly adopt and cite.

novelty.justification: Applying SAE decomposition to attribution/contribution vectors rather than activations, plus the sign-decorrelation finding, is a genuinely new angle, though it composes existing IG and SAE machinery.

rigor.justification: Method is valid and the perturbation experiments test causality directly, but several choices (10 IG steps, top-logit target, 0.2 threshold) are underjustified.

statistical_soundness.justification: No error bars, seed variance, or significance tests on any headline comparison; key claims rest on single-model, single-exemplar-class displays.

calibration_honesty.justification: Limitations section is real, ViT underperformance is admitted, speculative explanations are flagged; minor overreach in the LLM aside and abstract framing.

clarity.justification: Frequent run-on sentences, typos, garbled math, and an internal 200-vs-300-epoch inconsistency make the paper harder to read than it should be.

structure_compliance.justification: Standard structure and reasonable length; related work is woven into the introduction rather than a dedicated section but the flow is logical.

reproducibility.justification: Key hyperparameters (threshold 0.9, 3x dictionary, lr 5e-5, batch 128, L1 5e-5, 50k images, IG with 10 steps) are given, but encoder architecture details, IG baseline, and the epoch inconsistency leave gaps.

related_work.justification: Saliency and retina-modeling prior work is cited fairly, but engagement with the modern SAE/mechanistic-interpretability literature — the closest relatives — is thin.

figure_quality.justification: Captions describe informative, claim-bearing displays (layerwise trend plots, target/off-target perturbation curves, IRF examples) rather than decoration.

breadth_generality.justification: One main CNN architecture with block-limited analyses, weaker ViT results, and a single small retinal model only partially support the claimed architectural generality.

overall_recommendation.justification: Borderline accept: a novel, causally validated interpretability method held back by missing statistics, limited baselines, and substandard writing.
